text: ## City General Hospital — Appointment Policy

## Scheduling Appointments

Appointments can be scheduled through the following channels:
- **Online Patient Portal:** Available 24/7 for registered patients. Appointments can be booked up to 30 days in advance.
- **Phone:** Call the central scheduling line at (555) 100-2000, available Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM.
- **In Person:** Visit the registration desk at the main lobby during business hours.

## Types of Appointments

- **New Patient Visit:** First-time visits with a physician typically last 45-60 minutes. Additional paperwork and registration time of 15-20 minutes should be expected.
- **Follow-Up Visit:** Subsequent visits are typically 15-30 minutes depending on the complexity of the case.
- **Same-Day Urgent Visit:** Available on a limited, first-come-first-served basis for conditions that need prompt attention but are not emergencies. Same-day slots open at 7:00 AM each morning.
- **Telehealth Visit:** Virtual consultations are available for select departments (Neurology, Internal Medicine, Pediatrics). Patients must have a stable internet connection and a device with camera and microphone.

## Referrals

Some specialist departments require a referral from a primary care physician or another specialist. Departments that typically require referral include:
- Cardiology (recommended but not mandatory)
- Neurology (required for new patients)
- Orthopedics — Sports Medicine (recommended)

The Emergency Department, Pediatrics, and Internal Medicine do not require referrals.

## Cancellation and Rescheduling Policy

- Appointments must be cancelled or rescheduled at least 24 hours in advance.
- Cancellations made less than 24 hours before the appointment may incur a no-show fee of $50.
- Three consecutive no-shows within a 12-month period may result in discharge from the physician's patient panel.
- To cancel or reschedule, call (555) 100-2000 or use the patient portal.

## Late Arrival Policy

- Patients who arrive more than 15 minutes late for their appointment may need to reschedule.
- The decision to accommodate late arrivals is at the discretion of the physician and clinic schedule.

## Insurance Verification

- Insurance verification is recommended at least 48 hours before your appointment.
- If your insurance plan changes, notify the scheduling team before your visit to avoid billing issues.
- Co-pays and deductibles are collected at the time of the visit.
## City General Hospital — Department Descriptions

## Cardiology Department

The Cardiology Department specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of heart and cardiovascular conditions. Services include echocardiography, stress testing, cardiac catheterization, electrophysiology studies, and heart failure management. The department is equipped with a state-of-the-art cardiac catheterization lab and a dedicated cardiac intensive care unit (CICU). Referrals from primary care physicians are recommended but not required for outpatient consultations. The department operates Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, with emergency cardiac care available 24/7 through the Emergency Department.

## Orthopedics Department

The Orthopedics Department provides comprehensive musculoskeletal care including joint replacement surgery, sports medicine, fracture management, spine surgery, and hand surgery. The department features advanced imaging facilities, a dedicated physical therapy rehabilitation center, and a minimally invasive surgery suite. Walk-in clinics are available for acute injuries on weekday mornings. Elective consultations require an appointment. The department is located on the third floor, Wing C.

## Neurology Department

The Neurology Department evaluates and treats disorders of the brain, spinal cord, and nervous system. Common conditions treated include stroke, epilepsy, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, migraines, and neuropathies. The department offers EEG monitoring, nerve conduction studies, and a comprehensive stroke center with rapid-response protocols. Telehealth consultations are available for follow-up visits. Operating hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM.

## Pediatrics Department

The Pediatrics Department provides medical care for infants, children, and adolescents up to age 18. Services include well-child checkups, immunizations, developmental screenings, and management of acute and chronic childhood illnesses. The department has a child-friendly waiting area and playroom. A pediatric emergency section is co-located within the main Emergency Department with specialized pediatric nurses available around the clock. Appointments can be booked online or via phone.

## General Surgery Department

The General Surgery Department performs a wide range of surgical procedures including appendectomies, hernia repairs, gallbladder removal, and various abdominal surgeries. The department supports both open and laparoscopic minimally invasive techniques. Pre-surgical consultations are mandatory. Patients receive detailed pre-operative instructions and are assigned a surgical coordinator for scheduling. The operating suite is located on the fourth floor.

## Emergency Department

The Emergency Department (ED) is open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. It handles all acute medical conditions, trauma cases, and psychiatric emergencies. The ED includes a rapid triage area, trauma bays, a fast-track section for minor injuries, and a dedicated pediatric emergency zone. Average wait time for non-critical cases is approximately 45 minutes, though this varies based on patient volume. Patients are seen in order of medical severity, not arrival time.

## Radiology Department

The Radiology Department offers a full suite of diagnostic imaging services including X-ray, ultrasound, CT scan, MRI, mammography, and fluoroscopy. Contrast-enhanced studies require prior scheduling and may require fasting. Results are typically available to the ordering physician within 24 hours. Walk-in X-ray services are available for emergency and urgent cases. The department is on the ground floor, Wing A.

## Internal Medicine Department

The Internal Medicine Department provides primary and specialized care for adult patients. Services include annual wellness exams, chronic disease management (diabetes, hypertension, COPD), preventive screenings, and referral coordination. The department also staffs the hospital's inpatient medical units. Appointments can be scheduled online, and same-day sick visits are available on a limited basis.

## City General Hospital — Emergency Services Guide

metadata.title: Emergency Services
metadata.section_heading: City General Hospital — Emergency Services Guide

text:
## When to Visit the Emergency Department

The Emergency Department (ED) should be used for conditions that are life-threatening or require immediate medical attention, including:
- Chest pain or difficulty breathing
- Severe bleeding that cannot be controlled
- Signs of stroke (sudden numbness, confusion, trouble speaking, severe headache)
- Serious injuries from accidents, falls, or burns
- Loss of consciousness or fainting
- Severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis)
- Poisoning or drug overdose
- High fever (above 104°F) that does not respond to medication
- Seizures

metadata.title: Emergency Services
metadata.section_heading: When to Visit the Emergency Department

text:
## When to Use Urgent Care or Same-Day Clinic Instead

For conditions that need prompt attention but are not life-threatening, consider our same-day urgent clinic:
- Minor cuts requiring stitches
- Sprains and minor fractures
- Moderate fever or flu symptoms
- Urinary tract infections
- Ear infections
- Mild allergic reactions (rash, hives without breathing difficulty)

metadata.title: Emergency Services
metadata.section_heading: When to Use Urgent Care or Same-Day Clinic Instead

text:
## What to Expect at the Emergency Department

1. **Triage:** Upon arrival, a triage nurse will assess your condition and assign a priority level. Patients are seen based on medical severity, not arrival order.
2. **Registration:** You will be registered and asked for your ID and insurance information. Emergency care is never denied due to inability to pay.
3. **Evaluation:** A physician will examine you and may order tests such as blood work, imaging, or ECG.
4. **Treatment:** You will receive appropriate treatment. This may include medication, procedures, or admission to the hospital.
5. **Discharge or Admission:** Once stabilized, you will either be discharged with follow-up instructions or admitted for further care.

text: ## City General Hospital — Insurance and Coverage Policy

metadata.title: Insurance Policy
metadata.section_heading: City General Hospital — Insurance and Coverage Policy

text:
## Accepted Insurance Plans

City General Hospital is an in-network provider for the following insurance plans:
- BlueCross BlueShield (all regional plans)
- Aetna (PPO and HMO)
- UnitedHealthcare (PPO, HMO, and Medicare Advantage)
- Cigna (PPO and Open Access)
- Medicare (Parts A and B)
- Medicaid (state-administered plans)
- Humana (PPO and HMO)
- Kaiser Permanente (referral-based only)
- TRICARE (active military and veterans)

For plans not listed above, please contact our insurance verification team at (555) 100-2005 to check coverage before your appointment.

## Insurance Verification Process

- We recommend verifying your insurance coverage at least 48 hours before your appointment.
- Bring your current insurance card to every visit.
- If your insurance plan has changed since your last visit, inform the registration desk immediately.
- For specialist visits, confirm with your insurer whether a referral or prior authorization is required.

## Copays and Deductibles

- Copays are collected at the time of service (check-in).
- If you have not met your annual deductible, you may be responsible for a larger portion of the charges.
- The hospital will bill your insurance first. Any remaining patient responsibility will be billed to you within 30 days.

## Prior Authorization

Certain services require prior authorization from your insurance company before they can be performed. These commonly include:
- Advanced imaging (MRI, CT scan with contrast)
- Elective surgical procedures
- Specialty referrals (depending on your plan type)
- Certain prescription medications

Our authorization team will work with your insurance company to obtain approval. This process may take 3-5 business days. Please plan accordingly.

## Out-of-Network Services

If City General Hospital is out-of-network for your insurance plan:
- You may still receive services, but your out-of-pocket costs will likely be higher.
- The No Surprises Act protects patients from surprise bills for emergency services and certain non-emergency services at in-network facilities performed by out-of-network providers.
- You will receive a Good Faith Estimate of costs before non-emergency out-of-network services are rendered.

## Financial Assistance for Underinsured Patients

Patients with high deductibles or limited coverage may qualify for:
- Sliding-scale fee reductions based on household income.
- Charity care programs for qualifying individuals and families.
- Interest-free payment plans for balances over $500.

Contact the Financial Counseling office at (555) 100-2006 for assistance.
## City General Hospital — Patient Rights and Responsibilities

metadata.title: Patient Rights
metadata.section_heading: City General Hospital — Patient Rights and Responsibilities

text: ## Your Rights as a Patient

## Right to Quality Care

You have the right to receive considerate, respectful, and quality medical care regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, religion, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, or ability to pay.

## Right to Information

You have the right to receive complete and current information about your diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis in terms you can understand. Interpretation services are provided at no charge.

## Right to Privacy and Confidentiality

Your medical records and personal health information are confidential and protected under HIPAA. Information will only be disclosed with your written authorization, except as required by law.

## Right to Informed Consent

Before any procedure, you have the right to receive a full explanation of the proposed treatment, its risks, benefits, alternatives, and the consequences of refusing treatment.

## Right to Participate in Care Decisions

You have the right to participate in all decisions regarding your healthcare, including the right to request a second opinion.

metadata.title: Patient Rights
metadata.section_heading: Right to Participate in Care Decisions

text:
## Right to Advance Directives

You have the right to create advance directives specifying your wishes regarding medical treatment if you become unable to communicate.

## Right to Complain

You have the right to voice complaints about your care without fear of retaliation via the Patient Relations office.
## Your Responsibilities as a Patient

## Provide Accurate Information

Provide accurate and complete information about your health status, medical history, medications, and allergies.

## Follow Treatment Plans

Follow the treatment plan recommended by your healthcare team, including medications and follow-up appointments.

## Respect Others

Treat hospital staff, other patients, and visitors with courtesy and respect.

## Financial Obligations

Meet your financial obligations including copays, deductibles, and balances not covered by insurance.

## City General Hospital — Surgery Preparation Instructions

metadata.title: Surgery Preparation
metadata.section_heading: City General Hospital — Surgery Preparation Instructions

text: ## Before Your Surgery

## Pre-Operative Consultation

All elective surgery patients must attend a pre-operative consultation at least 7 days before the scheduled surgery date. During this visit, your surgeon will review the procedure, discuss risks and benefits, and answer your questions. You will also meet with an anesthesiologist if your surgery requires general anesthesia.

## Required Pre-Operative Tests

Depending on your age and medical history, you may need the following tests before surgery:
- Blood work (complete blood count, metabolic panel, coagulation studies)
- Chest X-ray (for patients over 50 or with respiratory conditions)
- ECG/EKG (for patients over 40 or with cardiac history)
- Urinalysis
- COVID-19 or respiratory panel test (if required by current hospital policy)

All pre-operative tests must be completed at least 3 business days before your surgery to allow time for result review.

## Medications

- Inform your surgical team of ALL medications you take, including over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, and herbal supplements.
- Blood-thinning medications (warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel) must typically be stopped 5-7 days before surgery. Your surgeon will provide specific instructions.
- Diabetes medications may require dose adjustment on the day of surgery. Consult your surgeon or anesthesiologist.
- Take only the medications your surgical team has approved on the morning of surgery, with a small sip of water.

## Fasting Instructions

- Do NOT eat solid food for at least 8 hours before your surgery.
- Clear liquids (water, clear apple juice, black coffee without cream) may be consumed up to 2 hours before your scheduled arrival time.
- Do not chew gum or consume candy on the day of surgery.

## What to Bring

- Valid photo ID and insurance card.
- A list of your current medications and dosages.
- Advance directive or living will, if you have one.
- Comfortable, loose-fitting clothing for after the procedure.
- A responsible adult who can drive you home (required for all outpatient procedures involving sedation or general anesthesia).

## What NOT to Bring

- Jewelry, watches, or piercings (remove all before arrival).
- Large amounts of cash or valuables.
- Contact lenses (bring glasses instead).
- Nail polish or artificial nails (interferes with monitoring devices).

## Day of Surgery

1. Arrive at the Surgical Admissions area at your scheduled check-in time (usually 2 hours before the procedure).
2. You will be checked in, given a hospital gown, and have an IV line placed.
3. Your surgical team will verify your identity, the procedure, and the surgical site (this is a standard safety protocol).
4. After the procedure, you will be taken to the Post-Anesthesia Care Unit (PACU) for recovery monitoring.
5. Discharge instructions will be provided before you leave, including medication prescriptions, wound care guidance, and follow-up appointment scheduling.

## After Surgery

- Follow all discharge instructions carefully.
- Do not drive or operate heavy machinery for 24 hours after receiving anesthesia.
- Attend all scheduled follow-up appointments.
- Contact your surgeon's office immediately if you experience fever above 101°F, excessive bleeding, increasing pain not controlled by prescribed medication, or signs of infection at the surgical site.
## City General Hospital — Telehealth Services Guide

metadata.title: Telehealth Services
metadata.section_heading: City General Hospital — Telehealth Services Guide

text:
## What is Telehealth?

Telehealth allows you to have a medical consultation with your doctor via secure video call from the comfort of your home. It is suitable for follow-up visits, medication reviews, and many non-emergency consultations.

## Available Departments for Telehealth

- Internal Medicine
- Neurology (follow-up visits)
- Pediatrics (non-urgent consultations)
- Psychiatry and Behavioral Health

## How to Schedule a Telehealth Appointment

1. Log in to the patient portal at portal.citygeneralhospital.example.com.
2. Select "Schedule Appointment" and choose "Telehealth Visit."
3. Choose your department and preferred physician.
4. Select an available date and time.
5. You will receive a confirmation email with a secure video link.

metadata.title: Telehealth Services
metadata.section_heading: How to Schedule a Telehealth Appointment

text:
## Technical Requirements

- A device with a camera and microphone (smartphone, tablet, or computer).
- A stable internet connection (minimum 5 Mbps recommended).
- A quiet, private location for your consultation.
- The latest version of Chrome, Safari, or Firefox browser.

## Telehealth Visit Fees

Telehealth consultations are priced at $100 - $175 for self-pay patients. Most insurance plans cover telehealth visits at the same rate as in-person visits. Verify with your insurer before your appointment.

## Limitations

Telehealth is not appropriate for:
- Emergency medical conditions
- Conditions requiring physical examination or hands-on procedures
- New patient visits to certain specialty departments
- Situations where diagnostic imaging or lab work is needed immediately
## City General Hospital — Visitor and General Policies

metadata.title: Visitor Policies
metadata.section_heading: City General Hospital — Visitor and General Policies

text:
## Visiting Hours

- General visiting hours: 10:00 AM – 8:00 PM daily.
- ICU / Critical Care visiting: 11:00 AM – 1:00 PM and 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM (limited to immediate family).
- Pediatric ward: One parent or guardian may stay overnight. Second visitor allowed during general visiting hours.
- Maternity ward: The birth partner may stay 24 hours. Other visitors during general visiting hours only.

## Visitor Limits

- Maximum two visitors per patient at a time in general wards.
- Maximum one visitor at a time in ICU.
- Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult and are not permitted in ICU.
- During infectious disease outbreaks, visiting may be further restricted.

## Smoking Policy

City General Hospital is a smoke-free campus. Smoking, vaping, and the use of tobacco products are prohibited in all indoor and outdoor areas of the hospital grounds. Designated smoking cessation resources are available through the Wellness Office.

## Parking

- Free parking is available in Lot B (outpatient visitors) and Lot C (employees).
- Valet parking is available at the main entrance, Monday through Friday, $10 per vehicle.
- Handicapped parking spaces are located near all building entrances.
- Emergency Department parking is available in the designated area on the south side.

## Food Services

- The hospital cafeteria is located on the first floor and is open from 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM daily.
- A coffee shop is located in the main lobby, open 6:30 AM to 5:00 PM weekdays.
- Vending machines are available on every floor, 24/7.
- Patients on restricted diets will receive meals planned by the hospital's dietitians.

## Wi-Fi

Free Wi-Fi is available throughout the hospital. Connect to "CityGeneral-Guest" network. No password is required. Do not use the hospital Wi-Fi for transmitting sensitive personal information.

## Lost and Found

Report lost items to the Security Office on the ground floor or call (555) 100-2020. Items are held for 30 days.
